Q1.question_text: What do the fish do once they have moved away ahead of the trawl?
Q1.reference_answer: They keep swimming ahead of the gear at the same speed as the trawl for an unknown period of time.

Q2.question_text: When do flat fish notice the footrope, and how do they react?
Q2.reference_answer: Flat fish are aware of the moving footrope before it reaches them, and they move away before it arrives.

Q3.question_text: Why do the fish eventually stop swimming ahead of the trawl?
Q3.reference_answer: Either they become tired, or they become more used to the disturbance.

Q4.question_text: Which case is the simplest to study, and what does the evidence suggest?
Q4.reference_answer: The simplest case is that of flat fish on the bottom; the evidence suggests that the fish are aware of the gear.
